syllabusTopics: Biomolecules: Introduction and functions of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, minerals, enzymes and water
Cell: Introduction of cell, concepts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

Detail structure of eukaryotic cells: cell wall, cell membrane, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes, nucleus, chromosomes, cilia, flagella and cell inclusions
Cell division: Concept of cell cycle, types of cell division (amitosis, mitosis and meiosis) and significances

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
CRISPR enables targeted gene knock-out or knock-in in living organisms.
GMOs are genetically modified organisms with traits introduced through genetic engineering.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The first FDA-approved gene therapy (for Leber congenital amaurosis) was developed using viral vectors.  ·  Synthetic biology aims to create novel organisms for biofuels, bioremediation, and pharmaceuticals.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Germline editing (embryo modification) is highly controversial due to heritable changes.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: What is CRISPR-Cas9 and how does it work?

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Recombinant DNA technology: combining DNA from different sources  ·  Bioinformatics: computational analysis of biological data

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Types of Biotechnology  ·  - Genetic engineering: modifying organisms' DNA

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: CRISPR = genome editing technology.  ·  GMOs = genetically modified organisms.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Give an example of a medical biotechnology application.  ·  What are the main ethical concerns regarding gene editing?

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Distinguish between somatic gene therapy (affects only the patient) and germline editing (heritable).  ·  Consider the precautionary principle in biotech development.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Ethical issues: consent, equity, unintended consequences, designer babies

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Biotechnology combines biology, chemistry, and engineering to develop new products and processes.  ·  Applications range from medicine (insulin production) to agriculture (pest-resistant crops).  ·  Ethical considerations require balancing innovation with societal values and regulations.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: How might synthetic biology be used for environmental remediation?

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Discuss the role of international regulatory bodies (WHO, FDA, EMA).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: - Synthetic biology: designing new biological systems  ·  - Agricultural biotech: GM crops, livestock improvement  ·  - Medical biotech: gene therapy, vaccines, regenerative medicine

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ethical debates center on safety, accessibility, and potential misuse of biotech.  ·  Ethical concerns: safety, equity, consent, designer babies.
